\raggedright
\footnotesize The backward pass evaluates the residuals at the current iterate;
the forward pass is the filter line search that follows it, with accepted step
$\alpha$ and bk $= \log_2(1/\alpha)$ backtracks.  FilterDDP prints these two
halves one iteration out of step, because \texttt{iteration\_status} is called
before \texttt{forward\_pass!}; the rows here are realigned so each holds one
backward pass and the forward pass it actually fed.  The last row has no forward
pass --- the solver converged instead of stepping.  Regularisation never fired.
Every backtrack in the table was a rollout rejection rather than a filter or
sufficient-decrease rejection, and the solver's own \texttt{ls} counter records
none of them.
